title: Summer sublet
context: Listen to a conversation between two friends.

lines.t: So, I finally accepted the summer internship in Toronto.
That's great! But what about your apartment here? Aren't you still paying rent for June and July?
Yeah, that's what I'm worried about. My lease doesn't end until August.
Could you sublet it? My cousin's taking summer classes here, and she's looking for a place.
Really? That would be amazing. I'd have to check with my landlord first, though. I think the lease says I need written permission.
I'll give her your number in the meantime, so you two can talk.

questions.prompt: Why does the man mention his cousin?
options: She could rent the woman's apartment.
She also has an internship in Toronto.
She knows the woman's landlord.
She is looking for a roommate.
optionNotes: Correct: she needs a place for the summer.
She's looking for a place, not a roommate.
questions.explanation: He mentions her as a possible person to sublet the apartment.
questions.evidence: My cousin's taking summer classes here, and she's looking for a place.

questions.prompt: What must the woman do before subletting?
options: Pay the rent for August
Find a new apartment in Toronto
Get her landlord's written permission
Meet the man's cousin in person
optionNotes: Correct: the lease requires written permission.
They'll talk, but this isn't a requirement.
questions.explanation: She says she needs to check with her landlord because the lease requires written permission.
questions.evidence: I'd have to check with my landlord first, though.

title: Password problem
context: Listen to a conversation between a student and an employee at the IT help desk.

lines.t: Hi, I can't log in to the student portal. I think I forgot my password.
No problem. Have you tried the reset link on the login page?
I did, but the email goes to my old high school address, and I can't access that anymore.
I see. In that case, you'll need to come to the help desk in person with your student ID. We can update your email and reset the password there.
Where is the help desk, exactly?
It's in the basement of the library. We're open until six today.
Okay, I'll go right after my lab.

questions.prompt: Why didn't the reset link solve the woman's problem?
options: The link was broken.
Her student account was closed.
She didn't know the link existed.
It sends the email to an address she can't use.
optionNotes: Correct: it goes to her old high school email.
questions.explanation: The reset email goes to an old address she no longer has access to.
questions.evidence: the email goes to my old high school address, and I can't access that anymore

questions.prompt: What does the woman need to bring to the help desk?
options: Her laptop
Her old password
Her student ID
A form from the registrar
questions.explanation: The employee tells her to come in person with her student ID.
questions.evidence: you'll need to come to the help desk in person with your student ID

title: Essay feedback
context: Listen to a conversation between two students.

lines.t: I got my history essay back. A B minus. I spent three weeks on that thing.
Ouch. What did the comments say?
Mostly that my argument was buried. Apparently I spent the first two pages on background before getting to my point.
That's actually really common. Doctor Patel said the same thing to me last year. Once I moved my thesis to the first paragraph, my grades went up almost right away.
Huh. I guess I always thought you had to build up to it.
Not in her class. She wants the argument up front, and then the evidence.
Well, the next essay's due in two weeks. I'll try it your way.

questions.prompt: Why does the woman talk about her experience last year?
options: To show that the professor grades unfairly
To show that the problem can be fixed
To explain why she dropped the class
To suggest he ask for a new grade
optionNotes: Correct: her grades improved once she changed her approach.
She never says she dropped it.
questions.explanation: She had the same problem and solved it, which shows him what to do.
questions.evidence: Once I moved my thesis to the first paragraph, my grades went up almost right away.

questions.prompt: What did the man previously believe about writing essays?
options: The main argument should come later in the essay.
Background information is unnecessary.
Longer essays get higher grades.
The professor prefers short paragraphs.
optionNotes: Correct: 'build up to it' means delay the main point.
He wrote two pages of background, so he thought it was important.
questions.explanation: 'Build up to it' means leading slowly toward the main point instead of stating it first.
questions.evidence: I guess I always thought you had to build up to it.

title: Returning a jacket
context: Listen to a conversation between a customer and a sales assistant.

lines.t: Hi, I'd like to return this jacket. It's too small, and I haven't worn it.
Sure. Do you have the receipt?
Um, no. It was a gift from my aunt, so I don't have one.
That's okay. Without a receipt, we can't give you cash back, but we can give you store credit for the full amount.
Could I just exchange it for a bigger size instead?
Of course. Let me check. Yep, we've got it in a medium in the same color.
Perfect, I'll take that.

questions.prompt: Why can't the woman get her money back?
options: She has already worn the jacket.
The jacket was on sale.
She does not have a receipt.
The store does not accept returns.
optionNotes: She says she hasn't worn it.
Correct: no receipt means no cash refund.
The store offers store credit, so it does accept returns.
questions.explanation: The assistant explains that without a receipt they can't give cash back.
questions.evidence: Without a receipt, we can't give you cash back

questions.prompt: What will the woman probably do?
options: Accept store credit
Exchange the jacket for a larger size
Ask her aunt for the receipt
Choose a jacket in a different color
optionNotes: She asks for an exchange instead.
The medium is in the same color.
questions.explanation: She asks to exchange it, the store has a medium, and she says she'll take it.
questions.evidence: we've got it in a medium in the same color

title: Conference travel
context: Listen to a conversation between two graduate students.

lines.t: So, are you presenting at the student research conference in Chicago?
My abstract was accepted, which is great. The problem is getting there. Flights alone are almost four hundred dollars.
Doesn't the department cover travel for students who present?
They used to. This year they're only covering registration, apparently because of budget cuts.
Have you looked into the graduate student association? I'm pretty sure they have small travel grants. My lab mate got one last spring.
I had no idea. Do you know when the deadline is?
Not off the top of my head, but their website should say. I'd apply soon, though. The money tends to run out.
Right. I'll check tonight.

questions.prompt: What is the man's main problem?
options: He cannot afford the trip to the conference.
His abstract was rejected.
He missed the registration deadline.
He does not know where the conference is.
optionNotes: Correct: travel costs are the problem.
Registration is covered; no deadline issue.
questions.explanation: His abstract was accepted; the issue is paying for travel, since flights are expensive and the department no longer covers them.

questions.prompt: What does the woman imply about the travel grants?
options: They are only for students in her lab.
They cover the full cost of travel.
There is limited money, so early applicants have a better chance.
They are no longer available because of budget cuts.
optionNotes: Her lab mate got one, but that doesn't mean only her lab qualifies.
Correct: 'the money tends to run out'.
The budget cuts were in the department, not the association.
questions.explanation: She advises applying soon because the money runs out, meaning funds are limited.
questions.evidence: I'd apply soon, though. The money tends to run out.

title: Locked out
context: Listen to a conversation between a student and a resident assistant in a dormitory.

lines.t: Hi, sorry to bother you. I locked myself out of my room.
Don't worry, it happens all the time. What's your room number?
Three twelve. My roommate's away this weekend, so he can't let me in.
Okay. I can open it for you now, but I have to write it down in the lockout log. After three lockouts, there's a fifteen-dollar fee.
Got it. This is my first time, so I should be fine.
Great. Let me just grab the master key.

questions.prompt: Why does the man talk to the woman?
options: He lost his student ID.
He needs to pay a fee.
He wants to change rooms.
He cannot get into his room.
optionNotes: He won't have to pay; it's his first time.
questions.explanation: He says he locked himself out of his room.
questions.evidence: I locked myself out of my room.

questions.prompt: When do students have to pay a fee?
options: Every time they are locked out
When they lose their key
After their third lockout
When the RA uses the master key at night
questions.explanation: The RA says the fee applies after three lockouts.
questions.evidence: After three lockouts, there's a fifteen-dollar fee.

title: At the pharmacy
context: Listen to a conversation between a student and a pharmacist at the campus clinic.

lines.t: Here's your prescription. You'll take one tablet twice a day, with food.
With food? I usually skip breakfast, to be honest.
Then try to have at least something small, like toast or yogurt. On an empty stomach, these can upset your stomach.
Okay. And how long do I take them for?
For ten days. Even if you start feeling better after three or four, please finish the whole course.
Got it. Can I still drink coffee?
Coffee's fine. Just avoid alcohol until you've finished.

questions.prompt: Why does the pharmacist tell the man to eat something before taking the tablets?
options: To avoid an upset stomach
To help the medicine work faster
Because the tablets are hard to swallow
Because he should stop drinking coffee
questions.explanation: She warns that the tablets can upset an empty stomach.
questions.evidence: On an empty stomach, these can upset your stomach.

questions.prompt: What should the man do if he feels better after a few days?
options: Stop taking the tablets
Take one tablet a day instead of two
Keep taking the tablets for the full ten days
Come back to see the pharmacist
questions.explanation: She tells him to finish the whole ten-day course even if he feels better.

title: Early study group
context: Listen to a conversation between two classmates.

lines.t: So the study group voted, and we're meeting on Sundays at eight a.m., starting this week.
Eight a.m. on a Sunday? Well, that's going to be fun.
I know, I know. It was the only time everyone else could make it. Two people work on weekend evenings.
Fine, but don't be surprised if I show up in my pajamas. Where are we meeting?
The library doesn't open until ten on Sundays, so Priya offered her apartment. It's a ten-minute walk from your place.
Oh, that's not bad, actually. Okay, I'll be there. Should I bring anything?
Maybe your chemistry notes from last week. Mine are a mess.

questions.prompt: What does the woman mean when she says this: "Eight a.m. on a Sunday? Well, that's going to be fun."
options: She is not happy about the meeting time.
She is excited about the early meeting.
She thinks the group should meet more often.
She is surprised that the group voted.
optionNotes: Correct: the sarcastic tone shows she dislikes the time.
She is being sarcastic, so she means the opposite.
Her reaction is to the time, not the vote.
questions.explanation: 'That's going to be fun' is sarcastic here; Ben's reply 'I know, I know' confirms she is complaining.
questions.evidence: Eight a.m. on a Sunday? Well, that's going to be fun.

questions.prompt: Why will the group meet at Priya's apartment?
options: It is closer to campus than the library.
The library study rooms are fully booked.
Priya has the chemistry notes.
The library is not open that early on Sundays.
optionNotes: Distance to the library isn't compared.
Ben asks Nora, not Priya, for notes.
Correct: the library opens at ten on Sundays.
questions.explanation: They can't use the library at eight because it opens at ten on Sundays.
questions.evidence: The library doesn't open until ten on Sundays
